analyst.summary: Hindustan Aeronautics is India's dominant military aircraft maker with a record Rs 2.54 lakh crore order book -- about 7-8 years of current revenue -- almost entirely from the Indian Armed Forces, and strong returns (ROE ~24%, ROCE ~32%). But the stock's ~32-33x earnings multiple is being paid for smooth execution of the Tejas Mk1A fighter program that has repeatedly slipped for over two years because of delayed engine supply from its US partner GE, with only 6 of the needed engines delivered so far and first jet deliveries now guided to Aug-Sep 2026. About 30% of last year's profit came from interest earned on HAL's large cash pile rather than from the core aircraft business, and HAL was recently dropped from India's next-generation fighter (AMCA) program, narrowing its future growth options. Management's own guidance for next year is a modest 10-12% revenue growth. Given the price already assumes a smoother delivery record than HAL has actually shown, we rate this a Sell on valuation versus realistically achievable growth, while flagging that the underlying government-backed franchise itself remains sound.
